observations: Photo 0 shows a collection of used automotive components leaning against an exterior wall.
Two drive shafts with CV boots are visible.
A steering rack is positioned vertically behind the shafts.
A radiator or AC condenser with some bent fins is leaning on the right.
A starter motor is on the ground in the center.
A brake caliper and a pulley are also visible on the ground.
The parts appear weathered and are stored outdoors.

claims.claim: Sold as is, for parts, repair or recycling
claims.evidence: This is a statement of condition and intent.

risks.risk: The specific vehicle make and model these parts belong to is unknown, making them useless for repair without identification.
risks.proof: Close-up shots of part number stickers or stamped logos on each component.
risks.if_unproven: as generic scrap metal by weight

risks.risk: The radiator/condenser may have internal blockages or leaks beyond the visible fin damage.
risks.proof: A video of a pressure test or the unit being filled with fluid without leaking.

risks.risk: The starter motor may have a burnt-out solenoid or worn brushes.
risks.proof: A video of the starter being bench-tested with a battery.

risks.risk: The steering rack may have internal seal failure or bent tie rods.
risks.proof: A video showing the rack moving smoothly from lock to lock without fluid leakage.

proof_requests: Photos of any part numbers, brands, or manufacturer stamps on the steering rack and starter motor.
The make, model, and year of the car these parts were removed from.
A clear photo of the radiator's inlet and outlet ports to check for corrosion.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as the car parts described. Since the seller explicitly lists them as scrap for recycling or repair, they can be priced at their worst-case value as scrap metal.
